text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein says "I am starting to lose patience and I am concerned that we are at the mercy of events...Netanyahu's statements are not positive indicators and I fear we may steer away from the path of peace."
- Prime Minister Kabariti says "we hear something from Netanyahu and see him doing something else, we share Arafat's concern over the continuation of the peace process."
- First group of those pardoned now under review by cabinet; of 415 people, half have already served sentences.
- Crown Prince Hassan starts European tour on Monday, visits Netherlands and Britain to discuss bilateral ties and regional security.
- Jordan expresses disappointment over Israeli policies.
- Minister of higher education denies intention to raise university fees for undergraduate degrees.
- Private sector calls on government to intervene to get deals in Iraqi market.
- Overnight rates on dinar rise to 7.5 percent as result of increased demand and fund shortage.
- Jordan stresses rejection of Israeli settlement policies.
- Jordan voices grave concern over fate of peace process. King calls for flexibility, vision on part of Israeli prime minsiter.
- Kabariti pays tribute to bedouin, opens Zarqa adn Russeifa projects.
